                                     PROJECT NO. 58481

 RULEMAKING TO IMPLEMENT                         §         PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION                      §
 STANDARDS UNDER PURA 37.0561                    §                   OF TEXAS


                   COMMENTS OF BLACK MOUNTAIN POWER, LLC

                                     I.    INTRODUCTION

       Black Mountain Power, LLC (“Black Mountain”) is a private, entrepreneurial energy,

power, and natural resources company with extensive experience in sourcing, developing, and

operating projects across these thematics in both the United States and Australia. Black Mountain

has transacted on more than $2.5 billion of projects over 18 years, and one of Black Mountain’s

business units has originated as lead developer over 3.5 GW of energy storage projects across

Texas, over 2 GW of which are operational or under physical construction. We are currently

developing more than 15 data center projects across the ERCOT region.

       Black Mountain understands the need to differentiate between viable and speculative loads

requesting interconnection in ERCOT but emphasizes that this process be executed in a way that

does not bar credible large load developers with a history of successful investments in Texas from

development by creating unnecessary non-refundable security requirements. Additionally, projects

that have been subject to extensive delays up until this point at no fault of their own must be

prioritized in any large load interconnection study processes. We appreciate the opportunity to

provide comments on this rulemaking in response to the workshop and look forward to working

collaboratively with commission staff to develop refined, mutually agreeable language to this rule.
  II.   PROPOSAL FOR PUBLICATION FEEDBACK

Financial Security:

       The non-refundability provisions in both PUCT Project No. 58481 Proposal for Publication

and in Commission Staff’s April 13th memo in PUCT Project No. 59142 function as a direct tax

on doing business in the state. Requiring developers to commit non-refundable capital before

capacity is even guaranteed creates an unreasonable and unjustifiable financial burden on

legitimate projects. Developers are forced to risk losing millions of dollars simply for the

opportunity to enter a study that could ultimately conclude that no workable capacity exists –

ultimately penalizing developers for even attempting to invest in projects in Texas. This policy

must be revised to ensure that financial exposure is justified and tied to meaningful milestones,

not front-loaded as a fee onto a process that offers no guarantees in return.



Projects Subject to Extreme Delays:

       Requiring projects that were submitted to respective Transmission Service Providers in

2024 to undergo additional studies and delays is unacceptable. Developers have demonstrated

patience and commitment by waiting through an extended period of uncertainty with no resolution

in sight just to face additional delays under a new process that could delay energization for an

additional two years. Any process that results in 4+ years in project delays is unacceptable, and

therefore projects that have been forced to wait should receive preferential treatment. ERCOT has

an obligation to prioritize these projects, and kicking them further down the queue due to the new

Batch framework will kill viable projects. ERCOT staff should continue to work and advance 2024

projects that were submitted to relevant TSPs and have demonstrated financial commitment to
 deposits or studies, and commit that they are studied in Batch Zero, even if the current proposed

criteria does not accommodate the project’s regulatory progress.
                                  III.   CONCLUSION

We greatly appreciate the Commission staff’s work on this issue and consideration of our

perspective.

                                               Respectfully submitted,

                                               /s/ Rhett Bennett
                                               Rhett Bennett
                                               Chief Executive Officer
                                               Black Mountain Power, LLC
                                   PROJECT NO. 58481

STANDARDS UNDER PURA 37.0561                  §                   OF TEXAS


         EXECUTIVE SUMMARY OF BLACK MOUNTAIN POWER, LLC

 ● Financial Security: The non-refundability provisions function as an unjustifiable tax on

    Texas development, forcing developers to risk millions in nonrefundable capital before

    capacity is guaranteed. This requirement must be revised to tie financial exposure to

    meaningful milestones rather than front-loading fees onto a process with no guaranteed

    outcome.

 ● Projects Subject to Extreme Delays: Projects submitted in 2024 have already endured

    unacceptable delays and must receive preferential treatment under the new Batch

    framework — ERCOT should prioritize placing these projects in Batch Zero, even where

    current criteria do not perfectly align, to prevent the new process from killing viable

    projects that have waited years for resolution.
